events.subtitle: The Gilded Age: Part II — East Coast premiere of Jake Heggie's Fantasy Suite 1803
events.category: Chamber music / Contemporary classical / Cultural exchange
events.factual_description: Wolf Trap presents violinist Daniel Hope and pianist Simon Crawford-Phillips at The Barns on Sunday, January 24, 2027 at 3:00 PM in The Gilded Age: Part II. The program includes Dvorak's Sonatina in G major, Kreisler's Slavonic Fantasie in B minor, Copland's Nocturne, and the East Coast premiere of Jake Heggie's Fantasy Suite 1803. Wolf Trap frames the recital around the way European traditions were reimagined into an American musical voice and notes that Heggie's Fantasy Suite 1803 was commissioned by Beethoven-Haus Bonn for Daniel Hope. The same work received its world premiere in Bonn in 2022 and a U.S. premiere in San Francisco in 2024, so this performance is a regional premiere rather than a first-ever presentation.

en.why_it_matters: This earns a RADAR slot because the program has a real argument rather than simply pairing a famous violinist with familiar repertoire. Hope and Crawford-Phillips move through music shaped by migration and transatlantic exchange, then place Heggie's Fantasy Suite 1803 inside that lineage in its East Coast premiere. The Barns should make the violin-piano dialogue and the new work's details unusually exposed, which is exactly the kind of intimate instrumental context worth tracking even outside RADAR's jazz center of gravity.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for the afternoon if the DMV calendar is open. The East Coast premiere and the scale of The Barns make this a particularly good local setting for the program, while the work's earlier world and U.S. premieres mean there is no need to treat the date as a once-only historical event.

es.why_it_matters: Esta fecha entra al RADAR porque el programa tiene una idea concreta y no sólo junta a un violinista famoso con repertorio conocido. Hope y Crawford-Phillips recorren música marcada por migración e intercambio transatlántico, y meten después la Fantasy Suite 1803 de Heggie dentro de ese hilo en su estreno para la Costa Este. The Barns debería dejar muy expuestos tanto el diálogo violín-piano como los detalles de la obra nueva; es justamente el tipo de contexto instrumental íntimo que vale seguir aunque se salga del centro gravitacional jazzístico del RADAR.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente a la tarde si el calendario del DMV está libre. El estreno para la Costa Este y la escala de The Barns vuelven ésta una presentación local especialmente buena, pero la obra ya tuvo estreno mundial y estreno estadounidense, así que no hace falta tratarla como un acontecimiento histórico irrepetible.
